followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: the nature of the task and each model's documented strengths.

**The task** is a straightforward, factual informational request — listing differences between American and British English. It's neutral in tone and benefits from broad knowledge and thoroughness. It doesn't fall into any sensitive or specialized category that would tilt the decision.

**The comparison:**
- On general knowledge and instruction-following — the capabilities that matter most here — Plover scores meaningfully higher (MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 75.9, IFEval 89.8 vs 85.3, Arena-Hard 90.6 vs 83.2). These gaps are well beyond the 2-point variance threshold.
- Neither model's task preferences strongly favored or disfavored this kind of request (both rate "neutral-tone transactional requests" near baseline, 50 vs 53), so preference data didn't break the tie in either direction.
- Avocet's standout strength is "well-specified extraction/transform," but this query is more of an open-ended knowledge-recall task than a tight extraction job, so that advantage doesn't really apply.

So with no preference or task-fit reason to prefer Avocet, I defaulted to the model with the stronger relevant capability scores — Plover.
